title: A reader could read secrets through logs, the probe event and gaps in the config masking
description:
Several narrow ways a node reader (or an operator, for the kernel log) could reach data meant to be hidden. The `probe.run` event published the probe's target verbatim, so a target like `https://user:pass@host/` put the credentials in the event log readers can read and in the shipped logs. `GetConfig`'s masking left visible a `tcp-check send` payload (a Redis AUTH, for one) and the ACL patterns compared against `http_auth_bearer`, `req.cook(...)` and `url_param(...)` (session tokens, bearer tokens); and `ConfigHistory`/`ConfigVersion` returned the real, unmasked SHA-256 when the stored text wasn't available to mask, reopening the offline oracle JANUS-2026-006 removed. The previous-boot `Logs` call served the stored kernel log to operators (`Dmesg` is admin-only) and let a huge `tail_lines` read a whole boot of LOGS into memory, where the OOM killer hits HAProxy before janusd.

**Affected**: a node with an `os:reader` (direct or a Controller reader), or an operator for the kernel log.

**Fix**: the probe event's target has its credentials stripped; the config masking covers `tcp-check send`/`send-binary` and the bearer/cookie/url-param fetches, and blanks the SHA-256 when the text can't be masked; `Logs` refuses the `kernel` id unless the caller may call `Dmesg`, and a previous-boot tail is capped.

**Besides updating**: nothing.
